stem: A nonpregnant adult has a fasting plasma glucose of 92 mg/dL after at least 8 hours without caloric intake. How should the nurse interpret this result using ADA 2026 criteria?

options.A: It meets the fasting-plasma-glucose criterion for diabetes.
options.B: It is in the impaired fasting glucose range used to define prediabetes.
options.C: It cannot be interpreted because fasting plasma glucose is not used to screen for diabetes.
options.D: It is below the ADA fasting-plasma-glucose ranges used to define prediabetes and diabetes.

rationale: ADA 2026 defines impaired fasting glucose/prediabetes as fasting plasma glucose 100-125 mg/dL and a diabetes diagnostic threshold as fasting plasma glucose at least 126 mg/dL, with confirmation required in the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia. A fasting plasma glucose of 92 mg/dL is below both ranges, so D is the best answer. A and B apply thresholds that 92 mg/dL does not meet. C is incorrect because fasting plasma glucose is an accepted screening and diagnostic test.
educational_objective: Interpret fasting plasma glucose using current ADA criteria and distinguish a value below the prediabetes range from impaired fasting glucose and diabetes.
source_document_title: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_version_date: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Diabetes Care 49(Suppl. 1)
source_locator: Table 2.1: diabetes criterion FPG >=126 mg/dL; Table 2.2 and Prediabetes section: impaired fasting glucose FPG 100-125 mg/dL; fasting defined as no caloric intake for at least 8 h
source_claim_supported: For nonpregnant individuals, ADA 2026 defines impaired fasting glucose as FPG 100-125 mg/dL and the diabetes FPG diagnostic threshold as >=126 mg/dL; fasting means no caloric intake for at least 8 hours.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

correction_summary: Retained the 92 mg/dL fasting value but replaced the vague ADA home page and the unsupported wording 'normal fasting range' with the exact ADA 2026 prediabetes and diabetes FPG criteria. Rewrote distractors to test threshold interpretation without asserting that one screening value alone diagnoses disease.
